thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERDUTY — PAGER fired for service=inference-gateway region=us-west-2
Details: metric=5xx_rate value=12.8% (5m) threshold=5%
Tags: infra-errors-high, region:us-west-2

pagerbot: Escalation sent to primary oncall @zoe (ack required)

zoe: acked — i'm on it. putting status here. zoom if needed.

martin: i'm pulling the dashboards now (latency, error breakdowns). any recent deploys?

kai: canary deploy 3h ago to inference-backend v2.3.1 (small worker-thread tuning). link: https://deploys.internal/12345

anya: heads up — cs reporting increased 502 tickets from a handful of enterprise customers in SF. adding details to incident doc.

support-lead: forwarding CS thread: some customers see bursty 502s on high-concurrency requests to /v1/chat and /v1/generate.

martin: logs from gateway show repeated `no healthy upstream` and `502 from upstream` for backend pod model-worker-1-5. error snippets: 
```
E0321 22:10:12 proxy.go:234] upstream error: connection reset by peer
E0321 22:10:12 gateway: returning 502 to client
```
\neng-sre: initial hunch — model-worker pool hitting resource limits (OOM or thread pools exhausted) after canary lowered thread cap. also seeing elevated timeouts to model container.

zoe: let's try short remediation: scale backend replicas + restart gateway proxy to flush connections. doing now.

zoe: runbook commands I'm executing:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-backend --replicas=6
kubectl -n gateway rollout restart deployment gateway-proxy
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-worker -o wide
```

martin: watching errors on grafana (link). 5xx rate dipped from 12.8% -> 7.1% after scale started. good sign but still above threshold.

kai: checking model-worker logs: seeing frequent GC pauses and `worker pool overloaded` warnings. possible memory pressure.

anya: CS reports reduced ticket volume from some customers; others still hit. marking partial customer impact. adding to incident severity note.

eng-sre: recommend rollback of canary to previous worker-config if scaling doesn't resolve. if we roll back, do canary -> stable rollback with health checks.

zoe: agreed. give scaling 10 more mins. if errors not <3% we'll roll back.

(10 minutes pass)

martin: metrics: 5xx = 3.2% now, p95 latency down 200ms. still seeing occasional 502s for long-hold streaming requests.

zoe: okay we have partial mitigation. i'm going to enable a temporary traffic fallback to the older model-variant for streaming routes to reduce backend pressure. applying routing rule now.

kai: routing rule applied (traffic split 80/20 -> 50/50 older-variant). watching.

support-lead: CS update sent to affected customers: short blip, mitigation in place, engineering investigating root cause. tone: apologetic + proactive.

martin: logs look healthier; no new OOMs in last 8m. removing paging threshold escalation to PagerDuty (closing pager).

pagerbot: PagerDuty note: PAGER resolved by oncall @zoe — condition returned below threshold.

zoe: marking root-cause suspected: canary lowered worker thread cap which reduced concurrency headroom; under bursty traffic workers started failing, causing gateway upstream errors. next actions: rollback canary and run a bake with higher thread cap; create a post-incident ticket with exact timeline + RCA.

eng-sre: i'll open the rollback PR and coordinate. tagging @kai and @martin for validation.

anya: scheduling customer follow-up message after RCA.

zoe: handing off to @martin for overnight monitoring and RCA drive. context: scale + routing fallback mitigated customer impact; plan rollback first thing tomorrow; share runbooks and logs in incident doc.

martin: taking over night oncall. summary: partial impact, mitigated, rollback pending, monitoring threshold set to alert me if 5xx > 2% in us-west-2.

zoe: thanks team :thumbsup: — if anything spikes ping me.

(incident thread closed for active dispatch at 1845611400)
